articleTitle: A Comparison of Outdoor 3D Reconstruction between Visual SLAM and LiDAR SLAM
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive comparison between Visual SLAM, utilizing an RGB-D camera and ORB-SLAM3 algorithm, and LiDAR SLAM, employing a 3D LiDAR sensor and SC-LeGO-LOAM algorithm, for outdoor 3D reconstruction. Our evaluation covers their performances in terms of visual perception, computational requirements, accuracy, robustness, and map completeness in outdoor mapping. The results show that visual SLAM provides more detailed visual representations, while LiDAR SLAM demonstrates advantages in efficiency, robustness, and overall map reconstruction for outdoor environments. Hence, LiDAR SLAM is deemed more suitable for outdoor mapping applications, particularly for robotics and autonomous systems navigation in complex outdoor environments.

articleTitle: Cyber-Attack detection of Bias Injection Attacks using Extended State Kalman Filters
abstract: Cyber-Attacks against Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) in Industry have increased in frequency and scale over the past decade. Successful attacks have damaged infrastructure and the quality of life for many. To help remedy this situation, we evaluate the viability of using a bank of Extended State Kalman Filters (ESKFs) to detect bias attacks, a class of False Data Injection attacks, on a linear time-invariant system CPS with mismatched disturbance. Due to its ubiquity in robotics, we used a DC motor model as the example model. Then, we designed a Dynamic Surface Control (DSC) based controller and an Extended State Observer to accurately control the motor’s position under the effect of the load disturbance. The sensors’ signals were then attacked by injecting a bias into the model’s output. Finally, the various estimates produced by the ESKFs were examined to identify traits possessed by an attack.

articleTitle: Outdoor Positioning Based on ROS LiDAR Navigation Compared with RTK GPS Accuracy
abstract: This study proposes the ROS 1 framework and a 2D LiDAR employed two algorithms based on particle filtering for SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping). The algorithms include gmapping (Grid-based FastSLAM Mapping) and adaptive Monte Carlo localization (AMCL) to establish maps and determine the positions for the robot navigation. Gmapping disperses particles generated by the 2D LiDAR throughout the environment, calculates particle weights, and then constructs a map by drawing these particles. AMCL matches them with known maps to estimate the robot's position. The navigation is carried out using the move_base for the analysis of six outdoor positioning points of the 2D LiDAR navigation robot, and the comparison uses RTK-GPS as the reference point. The target aims to measure the errors of the 2D LiDAR navigation robot concerning these six points. The comparison shows that the root mean square (RMS) errors of RTK-GPS are consistently smaller than those of 2D LiDAR.

articleTitle: Using Sequence Pattern Mining to Analyze the Associations among Air Quality Monitoring Stations in Southern Taiwan
abstract: Air pollution has the characteristics of multiple sources, various scales, and cross-regional distribution, making it impossible to be solved solely through pollution prevention and treatment in individual counties or cities. Therefore, for the study of air pollution, Sequence pattern mining is suitable to analyze the relationship between air pollution and regions. Due to the fact that most previous research has mainly used the level intervals of individual air pollutants and their monitoring values as the basis for regional correlations, rarely utilizing the level intervals of multiple air pollutants along with the monitoring values of a single air pollutant as the basis for regional relationships, this study uses the data of PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf>, PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>, and 8-hour moving average of ozone (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-8Hr) with Air Quality Index (AQI) sub-indices greater than 101 in the southern region of Taiwan from 2020 to 2022 as the basis, aiming to uncover relationships in the southern region of Taiwan and contribute to future air quality management.

articleTitle: Quadrotor UAV with Independent Yaw Control Using Sliding-Mode under Special Orthogonal Group SO(3) Attitude Representation
abstract: This paper focus on the development of control strategies for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using decoupled attitude dynamics based on Special Orthogonal Group SO(3) attitude representations. A sliding surface is designed for attitude and position control. To enhance the disturbance rejection, a time-varying integral gain is designed to rapidly converge the error onto the sliding surface,. By numerical simulations, the controller based on SO(3) with sliding mode control and time varying gain is presented.

articleTitle: Robust Object Detection Model for UAV Application
abstract: Not only common issues on object detection task need to be deal with, for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) applications, small object is one of the critical problems that needs to be solved. YOLOv7 is a powerful network architecture that provides high efficiency and accuracy object detection results. This paper adopts YOLOv7 as an object detection model for two different kinds of targets, one is vehicle, and the other is ocean flotsam. By training the model with open datasets and fine-tuning the model with self-collected datasets, we prove through sequences collected from real-world scenarios that YOLOv7 is able to provide robust and accurate object detection results, including vehicles and ocean flotsam, with real-time efficiency. Based on such experimental result, we confirmed that YOLOv7 can be the baseline for object detection model development.

articleTitle: A Design for Improvement of Visual SLAM in Dynamic Environments Using Feature-Point Removal of Moving Persons
abstract: This paper presents a design to improve the robustness of visual SLAM(vSLAM). A processing step of feature-removal is added to the tracking thread of the conventional ORB-SLAM2 algorithm to improve the localization accuracy of a mobile robot in an environment with moving persons. Instance segmentation and motion tracking are intergrated to identify motion state of people in an image. ORB feature points belonging to moving persons are removed for further processing of the vSLAM pipeline. The advantage of this method is that the vSLAM can remove feature points of moving people, while retain those belonging to static people in the environment, which improves the accuracy of robot pose estimation. The improved ORB-SLAM2 algorithm has been implemented in a NVIDIA Xavier embedded system, which is integrated to a mobile robot. In practical robot navigation experiments, the average positioning error of the proposed method is within 4cm for 22.4m travel distance. Compared with conventional ORB-SLAM2, the average accuracy of our vSLAM method improves 97% in a dynamic environment with moving people.

articleTitle: Lidar-Inertial Based Localization and Collision Avoidance in Unmanned Vehicles via Control Barrier Functions
abstract: To enhance localization reliability, we apply tightly-coupled methods that improve estimation precision through sensor integration, enabling real-time spatial awareness. To tackle realtime collision avoidance with unknown obstacles in the environment, we utilize Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) to ensure a safe distance is maintained between the vehicle and obstacles, allowing secure missions in dynamic environments. The integration of CBF with localization and path planning significantly enhances overall safety and enables real-time obstacle avoidance for unmanned vehicle navigation, particularly in scenarios with unforeseen obstacles. The proposed framework dynamically adjusts vehicle commands to avoid collisions, ensuring both reliable and safe operations. Simulations were conducted to verify the effectiveness of the developed controller.

articleTitle: Camera-Only Perception System for Traffic Jam Assistance
abstract: Traditional perception systems for TJA (Traffic Jam Assistance) are mostly implemented by fusing images with radar or lidar. As computer vision techniques become more powerful, cameras can almost replace the need for radar and lidar in perception tasks, which reduces the hardware cost of the system. In this research, we propose a camera-only perception system for TJA, which is able to provide the information of the vehicles ahead and the drivable area. The proposed system has been evaluated through real-world scenario sequences, and proved that it achieves high robustness, which is highly possible to be adopted for TJA development.

articleTitle: Layout Optimization of Shortcuts in the Sortation Conveyor Systems
abstract: Sortation conveyor systems are used across various industries to help streamline the direction of objects from one conveyor line to another. Sortation conveyor systems are best suited for high throughput operations that generally receive mixed unit loads and discharge them to outfeed conveyors or designated locations. A shortcut provides extra paths to quickly sort parcels to destinations without long deliveries on the main conveyor. The main conveyor of the loop is unidirectional, while the shortcuts’ conveyor is bidirectional. In this paper, an algorithm compounding ordinal optimization (OO) and binary seagull optimization (BSO) is presented to solve the layout optimization of shortcuts in sortation conveyor systems. BSO is a nature inspired algorithm that imitates the habits of food-hunting seagulls. The developed algorithm is used to find the layout optimization of shortcuts such that the capacity of the sortation conveyor systems is maximized. Simulation results reveal the remarkable advantages of the proposed algorithm in reaching diverse optimal designs and improving convergence speed.

articleTitle: Interactive Communication Assistance System Based on In-Air Handwriting Recognition
abstract: The idea for this project was born out of the necessity to enhance communication for people dealing with either short-term challenges, such as those arising from surgery or illness, or long-term challenges, such as individuals with hearing or speech impairments. We've noticed that individuals with hearing impairments often resort to using sign language as a means of communication, but the responses they receive may involve gestures or partial interpretation of body language. Unfortunately, not everyone is skilled in sign language, which can lead to misunderstandings, misinterpretations, and difficulties in conveying precise information. This challenge becomes even more significant for individuals who temporarily cannot speak or hear due to medical conditions. Therefore, our goal is to resolve these concerns by creating a lightweight and user-friendly device. The proposed system utilizes Jetson Nano as the computational core, leveraging the Mediapipe toolkit to recognize the user's finger joints and gestures within the camera's field of view. It then employs OpenCV image processing and convolutional neural networks to recognize airborne handwriting. An OLED screen functions as the user interface for displaying restaurant information. The ultimate outcomes are showcased on this OLED screen and audibly conveyed through a speaker to facilitate communication with others.

articleTitle: Case Study of Robot Arm Billiards
abstract: This paper mainly studies the function of the robot arm to play pool. To perform this function, a special gripper must be designed, so we use 3D printing to design a gripper mechanism for playing pool, and design the drive and control circuits for the gripper. In addition, we also design a camera to be installed on the gripper to provide image recognition. This paper only discusses the case study of "one cushion" bank shot. Bank shot is a playing pool technique in which the player shoots the object ball into the cushion first, and let the object ball bounce into the pocket. This practical study is a mechatronic system of a robotic arm with special-purpose functions.

articleTitle: Robotics with Multi-Fingered Grippers and Deep Reinforcement Learning in Unity
abstract: Dexterity is a challenge in robotics today, especially when robots need to adapt quickly to new tasks or work alongside humans. Multi-fingered grippers with more freedom can help by providing stable grasping and manipulation. we uses deep reinforcement learning to let multi-fingered grippers learn from videos without manual control. They explore and grasp objects autonomously. To simplify reward calculation, we employ temporal cycle-consistency learning to train an encoder. This encoder turns images into feature vectors and aligns task videos for a reward function. This approach enhances robot adaptability and task learning. And the simulation environment in Unity make training can progress as almost same condition as in the real world.

articleTitle: An Optimal H2 Observer Controller Design Formulation and Solution Based on Chain-Scattering Description Approach
abstract: Various applications involving control systems often suffer from sensor-related limitations. Observers bridge this gap by combining sensed signals and computer model of a plant to improve control performance, despite sensor challenges. However, implementing observers can be complex and sometimes difficult to tune. To overcome these drawbacks, this study proposes an optimal H2 observer controller design using the Chain-Scattering Description (CSD) approach. Unlike traditional methods, the CSD approach directly determines the overall closed-loop poles from the so-called Standard Control Configuration plant. Notably, this paper contributes to improve optimal H2 observer controlling design formulations leading to effective weighting functions selection, crucial for the system optimal control performance, and practical application of the observed signal. The significance of this work extends to various engineering applications, promising advancements in control systems engineering, including the use of AI techniques for weighting function selection. Validation of the proposed approach using example is provided.

articleTitle: Development and Design of a Lower Extremity Exoskeleton Testing Platform for Adjustable External Load Conditions
abstract: Exoskeletons represent a human-machine loop system, and their performances are often assessed by designing various tests after being worn by a human. However, the high temporal variability of the human body often affects the objectivity of the assessment results and makes it difficult to reproduce the same experimental conditions. Utilizing the characteristics of stable robot motion, a bipedal bionic robot was designed in this study to facilitate the wearing of exoskeletons. When the bionic legs are equipped with the exoskeleton for performing test actions, the status of the exoskeleton can be assessed based on various sensor measurements. Additionally, a gantry structure with a vertical linear slide and counterweight block was also designed in this study. The bionic legs were affixed to the structure to provide stability during their motion and to introduce additional loading conditions. Finally, the validation was conducted by implementing a squatting motion with the bionic legs, yielding promising preliminary results.

articleTitle: Improved SSD network for Oriented Object Detection
abstract: In recent years, object detection techniques based on convolutional neural network (CNN) have achieved many breakthroughs and have been widely used in various object detection problems. However, rectangular bounding box representations are not suitable for ubiquitous directional objects. This study proposes a series of improvements to the SSD model to achieve multi-directional object detection capabilities. Improved SSD directly returns all vertices of an object instead of rotating or sliding vertices on the bounding rectangle. In the experiment, we combined unmanned vehicle and fuzzy controller to verify the effect of parking space detection.

articleTitle: Automatic Visual Effect Adjustment System
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the audience experience at live concerts by synchronizing visual effects with the music. We introduce an automatic visual effect adjustment system designed and implemented for real-life applications. Our method leverages wavelet transform in conjunction with a microcontroller unit (MCU) to capture and analyze the rhythm of live concert music. The visual effects, represented by LED strips, are dynamically modulated based on the extracted rhythm. However, suboptimal settings during wavelet transform may introduce rhythm distortion. To address this issue, we incorporate a music genre recognition system into our embedded setup to fine-tune the wavelet transform parameters. This recognition system converts audio signals into log-power spectrograms and employs a deep learning (DL) model to classify music genres. The output of the genre recognition system is used to optimize the rhythm extraction settings, ensuring optimal synchronization between the visual effects and the live concert music. The identified genre and extracted rhythm jointly drive the behavior of the LED strips, creating a visually immersive experience for the audience.

articleTitle: Efficient Structural Damage Detection Using Joint Vibration Signals and 1D-CNN Mode
abstract: In existing detection methodologies, identifying structural damage often necessitates the deployment of multiple sensors. This study introduces a novel approach to structural damage detection, focusing on the joints of planar steel frameworks. The proposed method aims to address the issue of excessive sensor requirements. Initially, we capture vibration signals from the joints using sensors. Subsequently, by analyzing the signal discrepancies between damaged and undamaged joints, we achieve the substitution of vibration signals from damaged joints. This method effectively reveals the characteristic features of structural damage. Furthermore, we explore various combinations of sensors and employ a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network model (1D-CNN) for detecting structural damage. In practical implementation, we validate the viability of our proposed approach using benchmark data from the Qatar University Grandstand Simulator (QUGS). Results demonstrate that our method significantly reduces sensor requirements, utilizing only 40% of the total count. Additionally, employing a single 1D-CNN model enhances detection accuracy to an impressive 96.53%. This straightforward yet powerful approach not only enhances detection performance but also optimizes sensor utilization, ultimately elevating detection efficiency. In conclusion, our proposed method not only embodies simplicity but also yields remarkable advancements in structural damage detection. It further optimizes sensor deployment, thus amplifying overall detection performance.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional Bird’s-Eye View Features Fusion for 3D Multimodal Object Detection and Tracking
abstract: With the rapid progress in autonomous driving technology, the integration of multiple sensors into autonomous driving systems has become crucial. Existing methods often use point-level fusion, where LiDAR point clouds are projected onto a plane and fused with RGB features. However, point-level fusion approach leads to a loss of semantic density from the RGB features during the transformation process. To overcome this limitation, recent methods have transformed RGB pixels into 3D space using depth prediction techniques, generating virtual point clouds. While this preserves the semantic density of camera features, it introduces challenges such as computational load and depth completion inaccuracies. In this paper, we propose a novel fusion method that unifies the representation of multimodal features in the Bird’s Eye View (BEV) space, preserving geometric and semantic information. We introduce the BEV feature fuse module to effectively integrate rich semantic features from RGB data into voxel features. Furthermore, we utilize the Focal Sparse Convolution module to enhance feature learning stability through position-weighted predictions, thereby improving the capability of point cloud feature extraction. Our fusion approach retains semantic features and enhances point cloud feature extraction. Experimental results on the nuScenes public dataset demonstrate superior performance in 3D object detection and tracking, highlighting the valuable application potential of this approach in autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Trainable Multi-Rate PCEN Frontend for Bird Sound Detection
abstract: Bioacoustics is an important area of study for its applications in conservation, biodiversity monitoring, and endangered species monitoring. As the use of deep neural networks for bioacoustical tasks continues to increase, developing methods for processing acoustical signals effectively is an important area of study. A key component to such processing is the effective elimination of noise from the acoustical signal. Recently, methods such as Per-channel Energy Normalization (PCEN) and Multi-rate PCEN (MRPCEN) have been implemented for this purpose. Based on these methods, we propose a frontend, called Trainable Multi-rate PCEN (TMRPCEN), that introduces a trainable functionality to the important parameters within these methods. Our frontend demonstrates improvement on both the PCEN and MRPCEN method, achieving an average accuracy of 85.23% and an averaged F1 score of 0.847 using 10-fold cross validation on a condensed dataset for bird detection. These results demonstrate the exciting potential of TMRPCEN for enhancing bioacoustical analysis for avian vocalizations and beyond.

articleTitle: YoLstm-FSN : YOLO-and-LSTM-based Indoor Fire Combustion Stages Detection and Identification
abstract: In fire rescue operations, tactical command and fire situation assessment are as crucial to a successful operation as firefighting and rescue work. Recognizing indoor fires goes beyond assessing whether a building is burning or evaluating flame size; it involves identifying the four stages of fire: ignition, growth, fully developed, and decay, each of which comes with distinct rescue priorities. This study proposes the YoLstm-FSN (YOLO-LSTM Fire Stage Net) model, which combines YOLO v7 object recognition with the temporal characteristics of long short-term memory neural networks (LSTM) to enhance the stability of fire stage recognition. Experimental results confirm that the YoLstm-FSN model achieves superior performance compared to pure YOLO v7 and pure LSTM, with F1-Scores of 0.86, 0.51, and 0.31, respectively. The proposed YoLstm-FSN model demonstrates enhanced accuracy in recognizing the four stages of fire combustion. Therefore, the YoLstm-FSN model demonstrates promising potential in the field of fire rescue operations and can contribute to the advancement of fire safety and emergency management.

articleTitle: Merging Decoded Results of Block Projection with Continuous Degree in Structured Light
abstract: The proposed method in this study aims to address the issue of interreflection in structured light scanning. Interreflection occurs when the fringes projected onto the object interfere with each other, leading to inaccurate 3D reconstructions. To alleviate this problem, the researchers employ block projection. This involves projecting fringes onto the object in a block-wise manner. By doing so, the interference between fringes is reduced, minimizing the impact of interreflection on the reconstruction process. Once the block projection images are captured, several filters are applied to remove any erroneous decoding regions. The median filter and standard deviation filter are used to identify and eliminate incorrect decoding values. Additionally, the Epipolar line is utilized to further refine the decoding results. To merge the different decoding blocks, a novel method based on the continuity of decoding values is proposed. This method ensures that the merging process is smooth and accurate, resulting in a more reliable 3D reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in merging different decoding blocks. The method successfully mitigates the impact of interreflection, leading to improved accuracy in the reconstructed 3D model.

articleTitle: Concurrent Path Planning for the End Effector and the Mobile Platform of an Autonomous Mobile Manipulator
abstract: The autonomous mobile manipulator (AMM) that is able to navigate complicated environments and handle objects plays a crucial role in production lines of unmanned factories and warehouses automation. Path planning is a crucial function for an AMM to perform various tasks in a complicated environment. Efficiency, obstacle avoidance, (nonholonomic) kinematic constraints of AMMs and smoothness of the path are important factors that should be considered in path planning. Moreover, we consider to plan the paths of the manipulator and the mobile platform concurrently such that they can move simultaneously to reduce the execution time of a task. This paper proposes RRT-Connect-based path sampling and midpoint smoothing methods for this purpose. By sampling the paths of the end effector and the mobile platform separately, the path sampling can be accomplished efficiently. Then, the simple and effective midpoint smoothing algorithm is applied to generate a smooth and collision-free path based on the sampled points in the previous step. Simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in complicated environments like a warehouse with obstacles.

articleTitle: A Study on Longitudinal CCV Flight Control System using Multivariable PI Control for Tilt Rotor Aircraft flying in Helicopter Mode
abstract: In this study a synthesis of longitudinal CCV flight control system using multivariable PI control law when a Tilt Rotor Aircraft is flying forward with both rotor nacelles tilted to about 15 deg forward in helicopter mode is proposed. First in order to secure the longitudinal stability, pitch rate feedback is used as a stability augmentation method. Where control surface is the small forward angle variation of thrust vectors of both rotors. Next in order to achieve the longitudinal CCV mode flight, those are, Fuselage Pitch Pointing Mode, Vertical Translation Mode and Direct Lift Mode, multivariable PI control is used as a controllability augmentation method. Where control surfaces are the elevator angle and the small thrust variation of both rotors. Consequently this paper can show advantages and disadvantages of multivariable PI control law. To overcome the disadvantages a synthesis of decoupling longitudinal CCV flight control system is restudied by us. Its details will be shown in near future.

articleTitle: Trilingual Conversation System
abstract: This paper describes the design and the implementation of a trilingual conversation system that is capable of speaking Chinese, English, and Hokkien (Taiwanese). The system is designed to fulfill the emotional support and companionship needs of the elderly population in Taiwan, which is expected to increase significantly in the coming years. To achieve this goal, the system is implemented on a humanoid robot called "Mobi", which allows for natural and fluent interaction with the user. The conversation system is based on a modular design approach, which utilizes the GPT model with Speech recognition and Speech synthesis to achieve real-time interactive conversation in three different languages and provide a user-friendly simple interface that allows the user to switch between languages and modes. Overall, this trilingual conversation system holds great potential for providing emotional support and companionship to the elderly population, multilingual interaction to break language barriers, and can be applied to various fields which will significantly impact the improvement of life quality and work efficiency.

articleTitle: Autonomous Swarm Flight Control of Quadrotors Based on Boids Model & RTK-GPS Positioning
abstract: Currently, many studies on drone swarms use centralized control methods that navigation calculations are performed uniformly through a ground station and then navigation instructions are sent separately to each quadrotor for operation. In contrast, this study integrates multiple domain technologies, including RTK-GPS positioning, MQTT protocol, and 4G communication, to propose an autonomous swarm flight control system of quadrotors based on the Boids model. This system uses a decentralized control strategy, which means that each individual quadrotor is not subject to centralized control. By using only three simple flight control mechanisms, the swarm system proposed in this study achieves autonomous formation flight missions with high coordination. During the process, each individual quadrotor in the swarm maintains a certain safe distance from one another. According to the test results of the quadrotor swarms experiments consisting of three quadrotors, the positioning accuracy of this system can reach 4 cm, and the execution period of the navigation algorithm is about 0.1 seconds. The system exhibits good control performance and stability.

articleTitle: Switching Chaotic Encryption and Decryption Circuits Design
abstract: This paper presents a two-mode switching secure communication system design based on linear unknown input filtering. In the transmitter design, a two-mode encryption method through unknown inputs switching is developed to enhance the security of transmitted message. Specifically, the feedthrough matrix of unknown inputs in the output equation is properly chosen to facilitate the design. In the receiver design, a new two-mode switching derivative-distributed unknown input filtering (DDUIF) is developed to decrypt the encrypted message. In this method, a two-mode switching reformed transmitter system is first designed to simplify the receiver circuit design. Then, the previously proposed DDUIF is used to recover the transmitted message. Next, to compensate for synchronization error, a delayed transmitted message and a delayed decrypted message annihilating signal are proposed to correctly recover the transmitted message. Finally, the usefulness of the proposed method is verified using an illustrative example.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Task-oriented Robots with Hybrid Energy
abstract: This research focuses on the 2023 SPDC competition project, which provides the necessary power for robots based on energy types such as wind and light. Under the guidance of many special restrictions, a competitive task-oriented robot was designed, and it must complete the task of carrying items in the planned field. In order to make it more intelligent, this study conducts experiments and analyzes the charging schedule, so as to formulate a feasible and better solution. From the experimental results, it can be seen that the proposed method can improve the scheme used in past competitions. Saves 32 % in charging time costs and provides 43 % additional scoring time. This also adds 1 kg to the total cumulative weight. In future research work, we will still consider more elements to improve the performance of the robot, making it more competitive and practical.

articleTitle: Digital Automatic Gain Control Design for Optical Sin/Cos Scale Signals
abstract: This paper utilizes a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) in conjunction with an Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) converter to design an Automatic Gain Control (AGC) circuit for the output signal of an Analog Optical Scale. The analog Sin/Cos orthogonal signals from the optical scale are first converted into digital signals using an ADC converter, which serves as input to the AGC circuit. A digital Schmidt trigger circuit designed using the FPGA determines the quadrant of the digital Sin/Cos signals. By detecting the peaks of the Sin/Cos signals, a series of peak values are obtained to determine the maximum and minimum values of Sin/Cos, thereby determining the required amplifier gain for the AGC circuit. Finally, the digitally processed Sin/Cos signals from the AGC circuit are output, and the performance of the AGC circuit is validated using the output results of a digital-to-analog converter (DAC).

articleTitle: Image-servo Robotic Manipulator Using YOLO model for Intelligent Fish Farm
abstract: Taiwan is facing the challenges of an aging population and declining birth rate, which lead to a shortage of labor in the fishing industry eventually. To deal with this problem, an fish recognition system is proposed to identify the locations of fishes and to count the number of fishes. For detecting the fish localization, a detection system using YOLO models is proposed in this study. After training the fish figures for 300 epochs, the mean Average Precision (mAP) reaches 0.924 with a detection success rate of 88.89% in the experiments. To identify the fish positions in the three-dimensional coordinates, the bounding box coordinate of the fish is determined by a D435 depth camera to acquire depth values by converting into the three-dimensional coordinates. In the three scenarios of the experiments, the results showed an average error of only 3.7 centimeters with YOLO v7. The field experiment demonstrated excellent performance with an error of 3.9 centimeters. Furthermore, a 3 D.O.F robotic arm is designed for the precise throwing task. Via a self-designed C# code, the robot is designed to implement the throwing task via the motion planning. Finally, the effectiveness using the robot with the YOLOv7 network is proved by experiments.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Characteristic Recognition System of Permanent Magnet DC Motors Measurement
abstract: In recent years, the lighting pendant system has played an indispensable and important role in many public spaces. However, daily maintenance and replacing hundreds of lighting fixtures in these high-ceilinged buildings become difficult. In order to solve this problem, many manufacturers combine lighting chandeliers with lifting power modules. However, due to the large number of lifting power modules that need to be installed, it is impossible to measure all modules' worm gear DC motors in the shortest time. Therefore, the portable measurement system in this thesis is developed through Raspberry Pi and Python, and data interpretation is carried out through a quick-release speed measurement mechanism and an acceleration algorithm built in the cloud so that motor measurement can be popularized in various use environments. While the system is not working on measuring, the software also contains an online data collection functionality to monitor the motor for a long time in the era of big data and the Internet of things so that this portable measurement system can fully exert its benefits in the industry.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach in IoT-based Smart Plantation Monitoring System
abstract: The world's need for food is an important aspect of achieving the sustainable development goals (SDGs) proclaimed by the United Nations. One of the techniques used in this effort is to integrate technology into the management of food resources. In this study, the integration of IoT devices with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models was carried out in a plantation smart monitoring system. The research stages are (1) Integrating all hardware components; (2) Validating an IoT-based smart monitoring system; (3) analyzing DRL models; and (4) implementing the recommended DRL model into the system. Testing was carried out in 2 stages. In the first stage, the level of accuracy of the device was tested, which resulted in an accuracy percentage of 97.40%. While the second test on the DRL modeling implemented on the system produces an accuracy of 97.8% with an initial parameter epoch of 160 and a learning rate of 0.01, the input layer consists of 3 features, the output layer consists of 2 classes (0 and 1), and hidden layers 1 and 2 consist of 128 and 256 neurons, respectively. From the results of testing the indications of an IoT-based smart monitoring system device, it is a recommendation for farmer plantations to monitor plantation areas remotely, precisely, conveniently, and at a low cost.

articleTitle: YOLOv5 based Intelligent Defect Detection of Dual-color Gradient Object Fabricated by Fused Deposition Modeling Additive Manufacturing System
abstract: Quality insurance is a critical process in the manufacturing industry. Additive manufacturing (AM) has gained rapid development due to its capability of producing complex parts. Among various additive manufacturing, Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is widely used by consumers and businesses. In recent years, deep learning has been applied to enhance quality inspection in the manufacturing sector by combining traditional AOI with AI, particularly in multi-class defect detection. This paper proposes an intelligent defect detection system for FDM dual-color gradient objects based on the YOLOv5. Traditional inspection methods may struggle to detect defects caused by uneven colors from the shape or material incompatibility of dual-color gradient objects. By integrating an intelligent defect detection system into the production process, accuracy checks and classification can be performed to detect and address issues promptly, thus reducing costs. In this study, an image database for FDM dual-color gradient objects with curved surfaces is established by an automated imaging system equipped with two cameras and two controllable lighting sources to enable multi-angle observation and quickly acquire the image data of training and test samples. The primary objective is to detect nine different samples, categorized into six defect classes: good(normal), curling, break, foreign, gap, and uneven defects. A total of 1914 images are obtained. The images are split into training (80%, 1531 images) and validation (20%, 383 images) sets. Testing sets are also used to evaluate the model's performance. The YOLOv5 model is built and the performance among different depth (s, m, l, x) is compared after training for 100 epochs. The built model achieves performance of over 90% (Mean Average Precision mAP@0.5) for the validation set. Furthermore, the model is tested under on-line FDM fabricating process to verify the application in real-time defect detection in the future.

articleTitle: Control Design and Implementation of the Dual-Drive Gantry System
abstract: This paper aims to study the different control methods and implementation of the dual-drive gantry control system. In this paper, the Euler-Lagrange method is used to derive the mathematical dynamic model of the system. The derived dynamic model is then linearized and decoupled for the control design. Simulink is used to conduct simulation studies of the designed control systems. In the mechanism design of the dual-drive gantry system, the system can be easily converted into a soft connection or a rigid connection enabling us to study the effects between these two structures. The control laws are implemented in the experiments through a digital signal processor. The decoupling control and parallel control methods are used to control the dual-drive gantry system with a load placed in different positions. The performance comparison of different control methods is made. Finally, it is shown that the proposed decoupling control method can reduce the load disturbance. Moreover, the proposed decoupling control method has a lower tracking error when the system is in the soft connection.

articleTitle: Optimization of Medical Staffing Costs in Hospital Emergency Departments
abstract: Health system managers should determine how to choose the medical staff configuration in each service within the constraints concerning the mean waiting time of all patients. Hospital managers wish to increase the utilization of available resources secured from their health services budget. Therefore, managers must construct highly efficient systems that can reduce staffing costs while providing the required level of care, such as maximizing patient satisfaction and minimizing waiting time. In this research, an algorithm embedding ordinal optimization into beluga whale optimization is developed to resolve the optimal medical staff configuration in emergency departments. Beluga whale optimization is a nature-inspired approach that depicts the behaviors of swimming, foraging, and whale falling of beluga whale populations. The developed algorithm is used to find the optimal medical staff configuration such that waiting times are minimized. Experimental results reveal that the developed algorithm has the capability of providing competitive and promising results.

articleTitle: Servo Drive Controller Tuning by Machine Learning Model and Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: This research aims to provide a novel method to tune the control parameter of an unknown system in a motor drive. The study aims to achieve better control effects by adjusting the external control parameters by incorporating an additional controller. In terms of parameter adjustment methodology, a machine learning model is adopted to represent the system. The model with an accuracy of 0.95. This model is then combined with an optimization algorithm (PSO) to obtain the optimal control parameters. Compare these results with the outcomes obtained from a numerical method for motor modeling, this method improves the optimization of the characteristics by 24%.

articleTitle: Position Control of Quadcopter with First-Order Fast Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Method
abstract: This paper discusses the position control and the design of the controller of unmanned aerial vehicles. We use the First-Order Fast Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Control to design the dynamic function. Prove that the error of position and velocity can be convergence and don’t need to consider the Lyapunov function. We have made several simulations with the First-Order Fast Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Control and prove that this design is feasible.

Author Keywords: First-order fast Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Control (FOFNTSMC [10])

articleTitle: Research on Optimum Improvement of Turning Surface Roughness by Ultrasonic Vibration Assisted Turning System
abstract: This research is to develop an ultrasonic vibration-assisted turning system and apply the robust process design method to optimize and enhance its turning efficiency. The first part of the study uses the finite element analysis method to analyze the natural mode of the (UAT) system tool and the horn and finds the maximum resonance frequency to effectively strengthen the vibration transmitted by the horn to the tool to obtain the maximum amplitude. According to the modal analysis results, the vibration frequency 19KHz is the closest to the Y-axis vibration direction of this study. The second part of the study applies the robust process design method to turn AISI 1045 steel and optimize its surface roughness. Knowing that the optimal cutting parameters are nose radius 0.4(mm), feed rate 0.1 (mm/rev), cutting speed 250 (m/min), depth of cut 0.15 (mm), the best surface roughness 0.74(µm); and compare the surface roughness with/without ultrasonic vibration assisted turning by its cutting parameters; the experimental results show that ultrasonic vibration assisted turning has better effect than that without ultrasonic vibration assisted turning.

articleTitle: Implementation of Deep Pose Estimator Based Emotion Recognition System
abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely applied in emotion recognition. To improve the large parameter configuration and time-consuming problems, a smart embedded emotion recognition system is proposed and implemented in this study. Firstly, a modified OpenPose is proposed to lighten the computational load. One stage of Part Affinity Fields (PAFs) is reduced, resulting in three stages for PAFs and two stages for key joints. After extracting the required keypoints, 21 vector magnitudes are calculated as the emotion features real time. Then a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) is designed as a classifier. To train the model, all the 21 vector magnitudes are used as inputs for the BPNN. The recognized results of the classifier contain six emotion categories. Finally, the proposed system is implemented in the NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX as a smart embedded system. Some experimental results are provided to prove its effectiveness. The future goal is to apply the embedded recognition system into companion robot to interact with the host.

articleTitle: CACS20223 Mechatronic Joystick Drive with Feedback for excavator
abstract: The purpose of this work is to develop and perform research on a universal joystick drive system for different manual hydraulic distributors and improve its operation performance by introducing a new mechatronic design and a control algorithm. To do this, research of various sensors will be carried out. Research on the operation of sensors in the joystick drive system will help further developments in this direction and can add additional functions such as automatic, tele-operated, or manual with dig assistance. Implementing a mechatronic system for hydraulic system control in existing excavators and other hydraulic driven machines. This new developed device and methodology of their implementation will convert an excavator into a robot containing 4 degrees of freedom. Research based on the original test bench, consisting of computer-controlled drives for hydraulic distributor manipulation of real excavator working joysticks. The development allows you to upgrade equipment instead of buying a new one, which reduces the cost of updating and makes it easier for workers, as well as allows them to work more efficiently.

articleTitle: An Optimal H2 Controller Design Formulation and Solution Based on Chain-Scattering Description Approach
abstract: This paper presents an approach for the design of optimal H2 feedback controllers using the Chain-scattering Description two-port framework. The proposed method enables a direct determination of the closed-loop poles from the state-space representation of a Standard Control Configuration plant. By leveraging the computer-aided design tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, the proposed solution facilitates efficient controller realization and analysis. The key contribution lies in the effective selection of weighting functions, which play a crucial role in determining the control system behavior. The presented formulation of weighting function selections aims to enhance the practical application of the optimal feedback controller design. The significance of this work extends to various engineering applications, promising advancements in control systems engineering, including the use of AI techniques for weighting function selection with the aim to drive innovation and enhance control system performance. Validation of the proposed approach using examples were provided.

articleTitle: Economical UWB/IMU/VO Fusion for Mobile Robot Localization and Mapping in Poultry House
abstract: This paper presents an economical fusion of ultra-wideband (UWB), inertial measurement unit (IMU), and visual odometer (VO) technologies for indoor mobile robot localization and mapping. Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) technology is employed to construct maps and collaborate with the A* search algorithm for path planning. The positioning information obtained from UWB is utilized to enhance dead reckoning and minimize positioning errors. The fusion of precise distance measurements, orientation data, path information, and real-time appearance-based mapping (RTAB-Map) contributes to enhanced positioning accuracy and robustness. Experimental results showcase improved robot localization accuracy and detailed environment mapping. This collaborative approach serves as an affordable solution for various applications, including the autonomous navigation of mobile robots within poultry houses.

articleTitle: Using Multiple Neurophysiological Features to Construct the Predictive Models of Lower Limb Motor Preparation Onset
abstract: Motor preparation (MP) is a state of brain activity that occurs for a short period of time before an exercise is performed, and it has also been shown that this brain activity is associated with neurological rehabilitation. However, it is not easy to detect this phenomenon in the lower limbs using EEG, so this study aims to construct a prediction model using multiple combinations of feature extraction, feature selection, and classifiers, and to find the optimal combination of results. In this study, 34 healthy subjects were collected to construct and test the unilateral leg MP onset detection model. PSD, PCC, and CSP were used to extract the features and find the best model combination for each of them. PSD was found to perform best when using mRMR for feature selection and a soft-voting classifier containing multiple classifier algorithms, with MP onset accuracy of 81.14±1.11% and 81.01±1.37% for the left and right legs, respectively; PCC performs best when using LinearSVM without feature selection, with MP onset accuracies of 85.46±1.24% and 85.5±1.44% for the left and right legs, respectively; CSP performs best when using LDA with feature selection, with MP onset accuracy of 81.77±1.6% and 83.29±1.57% for the left and right legs, respectively. The accuracy of all three features was more than 80%, which means that these three neurophysiological features have their physiological significance. In addition, we also analyzed the subjects' motor preparation data by MRCP and found that MRCP tended to be more pronounced in the senior subjects when they were in motor preparing. Perhaps this can be studied in depth and used as an EEG indicator in the future to be extended to the clinic.

articleTitle: An Exoskeleton BCI System for Stroke Rehabilitation Using Multi-modality Training Mode
abstract: With the advent of the global aging era, the impact of stroke on humans is continuously increasing. Therefore, new therapeutic approaches to enhance patient recovery are receiving growing attention. Stroke is a severe neurological disorder that causes brain damage, requiring extended periods of rehabilitation for patients to return to normal life. Currently, common clinical methods largely rely on traditional passive limb rehabilitation, primarily targeting peripheral nerve training. Nowadays, an increasing number of people are recognizing the importance of post-stroke neuroplasticity. This study aims to activate patients' central nervous system and proposes a brain-machine interface (BCI) exoskeleton system based on human cognition. By designing three cognitive brainwave training models, including an attention-based standing-up model detecting θ-band power decrease, a relaxation-based sitting-down model detecting α-band power increase, and a walking model detecting MRCP, patients can actively control lower limb exoskeleton movement using brainwaves.This study provides cross-validation accuracy through both normal subjects and stroke patients, with accuracies of 87.13±9.38 and 80.83±9.68, respectively. Envisioning a rehabilitation system guided by human cognition, our team has developed an intuitive BCI exoskeleton system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Running Motion Generator for Humanoid Robots using SLIPM and CPG
abstract: The purpose of this research is devoted to establishing a running generation technique for bipedal robots. The motion generator is based on the Bipedal Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum Model (Bi-SLIPM) and is designed to stabilize running motions. This work incorporates human motion features during the generator process. First, this paper introduces the bipedal robot used for the tasks. The 2D Bi-SLIPM is employed to generate the running pattern. To ensure the applicability of the running motions generated by the 2D Bi-SLIPM in real-life scenarios, this paper introduces the concept of Discrepancy of Leg Compression (DLC) based on the 2D Bi-SLIPM. Additionally, a Central Pattern Generator (CPG) is integrated as an auxiliary synthesizer to generate DLC-CPG motions. These motions serve as the motion generators for the abduction direction of the hip and the ankle. Moreover, to address the challenges posed by tremors and inherent instability in running movements, this paper proposes the integration of feedback data from an inertial measurement unit. The insights gathered from the inertial measurement unit are incorporated into a heuristic algorithm, which systematically explores and refines parameters for the gait model. Through this iterative training process, the resilience and stability of the running gait are significantly improved. Ultimately, the training results demonstrate the successful realization of the proposed motion generation and control techniques on the physical robot.

articleTitle: Improving Clinical Decision-Making with Polynomial Regression-Based Real Patient State Estimation
abstract: As science and technology continue to evolve, clinical decision-making has become increasingly important in the field of medicine. This process not only aids experienced clinicians in making critical decisions but also provides guidance for those who lack experience. However, in the past, clinicians had to rely solely on their own expertise and medical reports to analyze patients, resulting in a time-consuming process. To address this issue, a scoring model was developed that analyzes patient conditions based on each parameter's value using data collected by the hospital. By utilizing computer analysis, evaluations, predictions, and optimizations, a suitable model for clinicians and patients can be created. This paper proposes a nonlinear polynomial regression approach as a model for predicting patient health scores, which has been validated through computer simulations and fits multiple researches and clinical examinations. The predicted results have been consistent with actual results when using the model, making it easier for clinicians to make clinical decisions. In summary, this model not only analyzes patient conditions but also predicts patient health scores with the support of appropriate parameters, making it a valuable tool for clinicians in their clinical decision-making process in the near future.

articleTitle: An Intelligent System for Automatic Detection and Cleaning of Bird Droppings on Solar Panels
abstract: In solar power plants, the accumulation of bird droppings may decrease power generation efficiency and necessitate manual cleaning, which can be difficult in large facilities. This paper proposes a solution to this problem through an automatic unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based method for detecting, localizing, and cleaning bird droppings on a large solar power plant. An automated flight route is generated for a UAV to fly over the solar farm and capture images of the solar panels, which are then stitched together to create a high-resolution orthomosaic image of the farm. A new YOLOv7-based model is proposed, utilizing an attention module to suppress complex backgrounds and highlight bird dropping features, and an extra head is used to detect small droppings. To determine the GPS coordinates of bird droppings, an algorithm is developed that uses the azimuth angle and ground level distance (GLD) between detected bird droppings and a ground control point (GCP). Finally, a system for cleaning bird droppings is established using the travelling salesman problem (TSP) to guide the drone in visiting each detected dropping once. The experimental results have shown that our approach is successful in detecting and cleaning bird droppings on solar farms. Our system has achieved a high mAP of 93.91% in detecting the accumulated bird droppings on solar panels, and has been able to accurately locate the coordinates of the detected bird droppings with a mean error of 0.14 meters.

articleTitle: An overview of XAI Algorithms
abstract: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning, which have already found extensive applications in various domains, the challenges posed by their complexity and opacity cannot be disregarded. This paper delves into Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), a technology aimed at addressing the ‘black box’ problem of AI and enhancing decision transparency. We will discuss two primary approaches to XAI: interpretability within models and post-training interpretability. We will analyze machine learning models inherently possessing interpretability, such as decision trees. Additionally, we will provide a detailed introduction to prominent XAI algorithms like LIME, LRP, and SHAP, among others. This paper will explore the current state of XAI, its challenges, and its future directions and potential. We hope this research contributes to the comprehension and enhancement of AI interpretability.

articleTitle: The Indoor People Tracking and Counting System
abstract: COVID-19 outbreaks and becomes serious from 2019 winter. Taking body temperature, wearing masks, recording footprint and avoiding crowds become important tasks and require a lot of manpower support for the prevention of the epidemic in every. In this study, we have integrated the infrared thermometer devices to measure people temperature and the people identities through RGB images at the entrance of buildings. Using the computer vision and deep learning methods, we would like to build a 24/7 and region-wide coverage assistance system to automatically record the footprint of a specific people in the building. We also detect if people taking off their masks in the yard at any time. The processing videos are grabbed from the existing CCTV systems. The developed system also locates the crowd and calculate the number of people in a specified area, and the manager can know the number of people and control the access in real time. It will reduce the burden of manpower. In addition, we have optimized the system performance to handle multiple camera videos and to reduce the hardware cost at the same time.

articleTitle: A Combination Strategy of Saturated Yaw Moment Control with Specialized Active Front Wheel Steering for Vehicle Assistance and Active Safety Control System
abstract: This paper introduces an assistance and active safety control system that integrates Direct Yaw Moment (DYM) control with a specialized Active Front-Wheel Steering (AFS) system to enhance vehicle maneuverability under normal driving conditions while blocking excessive wheel steering from developing instability in vehicle later motion. The proposed approach utilizes polytopic Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) technology to account for changes in vehicle speed. The control system is designed using the Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) technique with input constraints, and further reinforced with a high-gain saturation method to achieve faster vehicle response to reference tracking demands. Simulation results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed control.

articleTitle: Stroke Rehabilitation Exercise Assistance Based on Deep Learning Openpose
abstract: Incidences of stroke among young individuals have been increasing, highlighting the importance of rehabilitation therapy for future recovery. Rehabilitation scoring scales have been widely used in the field of rehabilitation to assess various abilities. However, these scales often fail to provide a comprehensive evaluation of each patient's specific condition, as they may miss certain specific movements or situations. To address this issue, this study aims to establish a Stroke Rehabilitation Exercise Assistance System based on Openpose. The system effectively identifies crucial movements encompassing sitting posture, the process of transitioning from sitting to standing, and standing posture, achieving F1 Scores of 0.966, 0.947, and 0.706, respectively. The research involved 17 stroke patients with an average age of 68.5 years. Over a three-month period, a total of 77 test sessions were conducted. By employing the Pearson correlation coefficient, the study analyzed the experimental results from these sessions. The findings revealed a significant correlation (84%) between the time taken by stroke patients to perform the sit-to-stand movement and their scores on the Berg Balance Scale, indicating a strong association between improvements in rehabilitation movement time and the individual's balance function and fall risk. The proposed model's accuracy and correlation with balance function measurements show promise for enhancing rehabilitation outcomes and patient care in the field of stroke rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Application of Advanced Fluid Control Technology in Energy Saving of the Pneumatic Plug Tray Seeding System
abstract: This study aims to realize energy saving in the pneumatic plug tray seeding system (PPTSS) via advanced fluid control technology. The pneumatic plug tray seeding system was designed and developed for use with Brassicaceae crops. A mathematical model of the pneumatic system was established and both simulations and experiments were conducted. A fractional order sliding mode controller (FOSMC) was proposed to reduce control signals and achieve energy saving in the pneumatic system. A PC-Based real-time control environment was established using MATLAB/SIMULINK for trajectory tracking control. Results of the study indicate that control signals were saved 7.9% to traditional control methods by the proposed FOSMC with smaller tracking errors. High precision seeding was realized at a speed of 60 trays per hour, with a single-seeding rate of more than 95% and a missed-seeding rate of less than 3%. The feasibility of the system was verified through germination rate experiments. Energy saving in the PPTSS was successfully achieved in this study through advanced control technology, contributing to carbon reduction in agriculture.

articleTitle: On the Relationship between the Desired Feedrate and Contour Error Constraints for 2-DOF Robot Manipulators Performing Parametric Curve Following
abstract: Contour error is an important accuracy index in contour following problems. For servomechanisms with orthogonal axes of motion such as CNC machine tools, reduction in desired feedrate is one of the most convenient approaches to reduce contour error, as contour error depends on the feedrate. However, the above approach may not be suitable for the case of articulated robot manipulators with non-orthogonal axes of motion. As a result, this paper focuses on the case of 2-DOF servomechanisms with non-orthogonal axes of motion. In particular, under certain simplification assumptions, this paper shows that the theoretical value of the contour error of a circle contour following motion depends on the feedrate for the case of 2-DOF servomechanisms with non-orthogonal axes of motion. As a result, one can use this fact to design a suitable feedrate profile so that the theoretical value of contour error will satisfy the constraints.

articleTitle: Edge-Fog-Cloud Real-time Water Quality Sensing and Alert System
abstract: With the development of modern fisheries, there is an increasing demand for real-time water quality sensing, particularly for cage aquaculture. The study developed a sensor-equipped small boat powered by solar energy, used to measure various water quality parameters such as PH, conductivity, sea temperature, and dissolved oxygen. We utilized Arduino Mega 2560 (Arduino) and Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) for data collection and transmission of water quality information. The data transmission employed an Edge-Fog-Cloud architecture, and we also developed a web and a mobile application (App) for users to conveniently access the water quality data at any time. When the water quality data deviates from the normal range, the system will issue an alert to allow users to promptly investigate. Additionally, we obtained meteorological and oceanographic data from seven locations near the Penghu Islands from the Central Weather Bureau (CWB), which can also be viewed on the web and App. Finally, we proposed a predictive model called LSTM for sea temperature prediction. The model exhibited excellent predictive performance with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.50, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.65, and R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) value of 0.96. These results demonstrate that the LSTM model has outstanding predictive capability and is highly suitable for sea temperature forecasting.

articleTitle: Tool-frame-based Admittance Control Strategies with Application to Nasal Swab Robots
abstract: Nasal swab was intensively performed by medical workers during the COVID-19 pandemic, which unfortunately increases their infection risks. To solve this problem, this study aims to developing a robot to perform nasal swab automatically. An admittance control strategy based on the tangent-normal-binormal (TNB) frame is proposed to on-line adjust the path of the robot according to the external force/moment feedback, and confine the contact force within a pre-specified bound. Therefore, safety and comfort of nasal swab are enhanced. Experiments are conducted on a curved passage and a dummy. Quantitative performance indices are defined to evaluate the effects of the control parameters. The results show that the robot can automatically adjust its path to pass the swab through the curved passage while restrict the contact force within the pre-specified bound, despite inappropriate initial poses. Besides, experiments on the dummy show promising results for practical applications of the proposed nasal swab robot.
